images.title: Perimeter of a square
images.purpose: Show that a square's perimeter is 4 times its side q, the first formula in the chapter.
images.composition: One large square sits in the centre with the formula below it; wide white space on all sides.
exact_structure: One square with all four sides equal, very light fill, outlined in #2B2B2B; its four sides are drawn as thick edges all in teal #0072B2.
Each of the 4 sides carries the letter "q" at its middle (4 letters q in all), the letters in reddish purple #CC79A7.
A thin curved arrow in grey #6B7280 runs once round the outside of the square, anticlockwise, to show walking round the boundary.
Below the square, centred, one line "Perimeter = 4 × q" with the 4 × q in green #009E73.
No number for the side, no cm, no grid.
rejection: fewer or more than 4 letters q on the sides
a side length such as 7 shown
a different formula such as q × q
images.takeaway: The perimeter of a square is 4 times its side q.
images.description: A square with every side labelled q and the formula Perimeter = 4 × q beneath.
images.context: Shown beside the perimeter example and formula text.
images.teaching_notes: Walk round the boundary with a finger and count four equal sides.

image_decisions.why: The square with four equal sides makes the formula 4 × q visible before any value is put in.
